text: REST APIs are a common way for applications to communicate with each other. When designing an API, it is important to follow best practices to make it easy to use. First, create clear and meaningful endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also essential because it helps developers understand how to use your API. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can make changes without breaking existing applications. Following these simple rules will make your API reliable and developer-friendly.
